//: Hosting + Firestore config for the `gpb` flavor (project gpbstockinventory).
Used with `--config firebase.gpb.json`; firebase.json stays the smartshelfkart.com config.
Deliberately NOT a copy of firebase.json. That file serves a hand-authored
marketing site at / and moves the Flutter shell to /app.html, which is a
smartshelfkart.com SEO decision (see seo/README.md) and nothing this brand
needs. Here the app is the site: it is served at /, seo/build.mjs never runs,
and every path falls through to the SPA.
`functions` is absent on purpose — functions/index.js is a documented no-op,
and deploying it would put this project on the Blaze plan for nothing.

firestore.//: Same rules and indexes as the other project. They are tenant-agnostic; they gate on companies/{id}/members/{uid}, not on a project.

//: Extension-less paths ONLY. A catch-all `**` here is actively harmful:
Hosting serves a rewrite when no file matches, so a request for a
chunk that is no longer deployed -- say main.dart.js_37.part.js after
a rebuild renamed it -- comes back as 200 text/html instead of 404.
The browser then executes index.html as JavaScript, loadLibrary()
rejects, and every deferred screen shows "Could not load this
screen". Safari hit this and Chrome did not, purely because Safari
was still asking for the older chunk names.
RE2, so no lookahead: match paths containing no dot at all. That
covers /dashboard and /products/123 while every real asset request
falls through to an honest 404. firebase.json makes the same choice
for smartshelfkart.com and says so.

headers.//: Firebase applies every matching rule and the LAST one wins: this is the default, everything below overrides it.
Content-hashed or version-pinned by the Flutter build, so a year is safe.

The entry point. Matching is on the REQUEST path, not the file on disk, so this has to say / -- a rule keyed on /index.html never fires for the page anyone actually loads. Cached, this strands users on an old build whose chunk names no longer exist.
